transcript:
Header: 2026-03-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (CTO - Polaris), Elena Ruiz (Product - Polaris), Tom Wu (Platform Eng - Polaris)

Summary: quick sync to go over marketplace onboarding, reference arch, and joint solution packaging. Not a sales pitch, mostly technical alignment and action items.

00:00 Maya Chen: okay everyone can see my screen? say yay if you can, we'll just kick off.
00:12 Sanjay Patel: yep, we got you. thanks for setting this up.
00:18 Maya Chen: cool, agenda — quick intros, listing checklist items, the reference arch Liam will walk through, questions about VPC/on-prem and KMS, then next steps and cutover plan.
00:32 Elena Ruiz: sounds good. high level from our side — we want Polaris Cloud to list Redwood as a marketplace offering so customers can subscribe easily; also important for us is deployment options: marketplace listing should support both hosted API and a private, VPC-deployable bundle.
00:50 Liam O'Connor: yep totally. we'll need to clarify what you expect to surface in the marketplace tile — do you want a quick start that hits Redwood hosted, or do you want an AMI/container-based private deployment package?
01:05 Tom Wu: ideally both. most enterprise customers start with hosted for evals, then move to dedicated or private for compliance. but for marketplace we need to provide a one-click deploy for private tenants too — like a helm chart or cloudformation.
01:22 Maya Chen: that's exactly what others do. Marketplace listing has two flows: SaaS link + a deployable reference arch for self-managed/private. For the self-managed we recommend a container image + helm chart plus a short reference architecture doc.
01:38 Liam O'Connor: going into reference arch — (screen) high level: front-end proxies -> auth -> Redwood control plane (partner-managed or Redwood-hosted) -> inference workers. For private deployments we recommend a VPC with dedicated subnets, egress rules, KMS for keys, and an audit log sink to your SIEM. I'm going to share the diagram after.
02:05 Sanjay Patel: quick Q — when you say KMS, do you mean we have to use Redwood KMS or can we use our customer-managed KMS? some of our customers require key ownership.
02:18 Liam O'Connor: good question. we support both patterns. for hosted-listed SaaS customers, Redwood can manage keys; for private or VPC deployments, we support bringing your own KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS). we'll include notes in the reference arch for key rotation and HSM integration.
02:38 Tom Wu: how about audit logs? audit retention and format is a deal killer for some customers. We need to ship a standard CloudWatch/Stackdriver sink or an S3-based archive with redwood's logs.
02:52 Liam O'Connor: yes we expose audit logs via S3/CloudWatch/Stackdriver and can push to your SIEM via our forwarder. audit entries are per-request with token IDs and route metadata. note — sometimes transcript systems mislabel tokens but we'll supply the schema.
03:12 Elena Ruiz: marketplace listing needs some legal items too: data processing addenda, SOC2 docs on file. who owns the compliance artifacts?
03:21 Maya Chen: Redwood will share SOC 2 and security whitepapers; for the marketplace tile we include links and a short compliance checklist. We'll also share the standard DPAs.
03:30 Sanjay Patel: on the technical side, packaging — can Redwood provide a sample helm chart and docker images we can rehost?
03:38 Liam O'Connor: yes. We'll provide a partner-specific helm chart. implementation notes: recommended k8s version, resource requests, node type (gpu vs cpu) depending on quantization. For large models we'd recommend GPU nodes + our optimized runtime image. For smaller configs, CPU quantized variants are ok.
03:59 Tom Wu: quick follow-up — how do we handle model licensing/cust entitlements through the marketplace? billing integrations need to handshake with Polaris' billing.
04:12 Maya Chen: marketplace entitlements typically go through the marketplace provider (AWS, GCP). Redwood will emit an entitlement token we can validate at runtime; for deeper integrations we can accept marketplace signals (webhooks) to enable features. We'll add a step in the listing checklist to capture the entitlement flow.
04:32 Elena Ruiz: are there any blockers around network egress or private networking when the runtime needs to pull model shards from storage? we have customers that disallow external egress entirely.
04:46 Liam O'Connor: for fully air-gapped customers we do an on-prem package that includes model artifacts packaged into an image or local registry. For VPC deployments we recommend internal object stores (S3 VPC endpoints) or pre-pulled images. We'll document a no-egress path in the ref arch.
05:05 Sanjay Patel: nice. about benchmarks — we want to publish some perf numbers in the marketplace tile. what's the plan?
05:15 Liam O'Connor: we propose an initial benchmark on your staging cluster: 1k inference requests (mix of short prompts and long chats), capture p95 latency, throughput, token cost. Redwood will provide the harness and scripts; Polaris runs them in their environment and shares results. We then sanitize and publish a joint performance card.
05:38 Tom Wu: is there a recommended quantization level for the CPU variant? we've seen quality regressions with some 4-bit configs.
05:47 Liam O'Connor: yes — we recommend dynamic quantization for CPU small workloads and 8-bit when possible; 4-bit is feasible with careful QA. We'll include quality regression tests and evaluation prompts in the repo.
06:05 Elena Ruiz: small nit — naming on the marketplace tile. Please don't call it Redwood 'Hosted Infernce' (common transcription typos).
06:12 Maya Chen: ha yes, we'll make sure copy is clean.
06:17 Sanjay Patel: legal/process note — Polaris marketplace team needs a listing checklist for our internal review. That should include marketing assets, security docs, pricing SKU definitions.
06:30 Maya Chen: we'll send the checklist. includes: logo + tile image, 400-word description, quick start link, SOC2 + DPA, pricing SKU table, entitlement webhook URL, support SLA.
06:44 Tom Wu: on the deployment automation — can Redwood provide a terraform module or is helm preferred?
06:51 Liam O'Connor: Helm is the primary for k8s deployments; we can also provide a terraform wrapper that invokes helm/registry provisioning for non-k8s environments. We'll add both to the partner repo.
07:06 Sanjay Patel: integration points — we need an API that allows our control plane to call Redwood endpoints for provisioning; what auth method should we expect?
07:16 Liam O'Connor: service accounts with mutual TLS or JWT tokens. For marketplace automation, we often use a short-lived token flow signed by the marketplace provider. We'll include sample API calls in the doc.
07:32 Elena Ruiz: security review — customers will ask for RBAC mapping to their IdP; is SAML/SCIM supported?
07:40 Maya Chen: Redwood supports SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning; for private deployments you can map identities to local RBAC. We'll include the config blocks.
07:52 Tom Wu: any performance gotchas with KV cache and batching when running behind our ingress? we use istio and sidecars.
08:03 Liam O'Connor: batching can be sensitive to latency and headroom. With sidecars like istio you should ensure TCP keepalive and adequate egress throughput; we ship sidecar hints in the helm chart. For KV cache, we recommend colocating the cache with inference nodes to reduce network hops.
08:26 Sanjay Patel: good point. also some customers will ask about offline model updates — can we coordinate model rollout windows?
08:34 Liam O'Connor: yes, the reference arch will include rollout patterns (canary, A/B). For marketplace customers we recommend scheduled maintenance windows and an optional automatic fallback to smaller model variants during scale events.
08:50 Maya Chen: ok want to walk through a tentative timeline — initial artifacts (checklist + draft ref arch) by next week, Polaris provides network docs by 15th, benchmark run by 17th, follow-up cutover sync 24th. sound realistic?
09:06 Sanjay Patel: that's good. Elena?
09:09 Elena Ruiz: yep works for product. Tom will handle engineering deliverables.
09:14 Tom Wu: fine.
09:17 Maya Chen: any more questions?
09:22 Tom Wu: one more — billing reconciliation. If a customer subscribes via Polaris marketplace and then wants a dedicated Redwood instance, how do we reconcile usage billing?
09:33 Maya Chen: typically marketplace handles subscription and initial billing; for dedicated/enterprise we often do a post-sale reconciliation where we map customer IDs to entitlements and migrate billing to a contract. We'll add migration notes to the checklist.
09:52 Sanjay Patel: okay thanks.
09:58 Maya Chen: great. quick recap of next steps: Maya send marketplace checklist + links, Liam to send ref arch + helm chart draft, Tom to send network/topology, schedule follow-up 2026-03-24.
10:18 Elena Ruiz: thanks everyone.
10:22 Meeting end. (approx 42 minutes)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-generated — occasional misrecognized words (e.g., "infernce" for inference, "KV catch" for KV cache). Some proper nouns may be slightly off.
